subject: Calibrating title for L5 hire — Manager vs Senior IC
messages:
From: Greenleaf Talent <recruiter@greenleaf.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Candidate rec — Daniel Park (incoming L5)

Hi Tessa,

Following up from the screens: Daniel Park (ex-Greentech) is interested in the L5 role on Infra Serving. Attached his resume and a short note on why he might be a fit for either a Senior IC L5 or an early Manager L5 depending on scope. He has led a small team (3-4) for 18 months but his most recent work was individual-contributor heavy (systems/serving optimizations).

Key signals:
- Strong infra chops, completed a performance uplift project with measurable P50/P95 improvements.
- Some people leadership experience (mentoring + interim team lead).
- Prefers a role with technical ownership but open to leading a small team.

Greenleaf suggests L5 (senior IC) as baseline but flagged his interest in Managering if we have a team ready. Any guidance on title/comp band? I attached comp_band_reference.xlsx for your convenience.

Attachments: Daniel_Park_resume.pdf

Thanks — Sam (Greenleaf)

--
Sam Rivera
Senior Recruiter, Greenleaf Talent
recruiter@greenleaf.com
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate rec — Daniel Park (incoming L5)

Thanks Sam (Greenleaf) — forwarding to Marissa and Jonas for leveling input.

Marissa/Jonas,
Quick read: Daniel looks strong technically but ambiguous on management preference. We have an open headcount (HC-3421) that was hired as an IC role but the hiring manager is open to converting to a people-lead if needed. Two questions:
1) From a comp perspective, is there wiggle room to offer manager-level base for L5 without breaking band parity?
2) From an org/people standpoint, is it acceptable to hire him as Manager-on-accept contingent on full headcount signoff? We should avoid title inflation if the role won't actually own direct reports in the first 3 months.

I attached the comp band reference. Please reply with recommended title and compensation range. If we can lock a manager title, I want to keep the offer competitive (esp. because he's currently in market).

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Staff Recruiting Partner | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate rec — Daniel Park (incoming L5)

Quick take: Comp bands allow some flexibility at L5 between Senior IC and Manager if we use the top of band for base + a signing equity uplift. See notes below from comp_band_reference.xlsx.

- Senior IC L5 band: Base 150k–185k, Total comp typical 220k–280k depending on equity.
- Manager L5 band: Base 165k–195k, Total comp typical 240k–300k.

Recommendation: Offer Senior IC L5 with a base at the top quartile (180k) + modest sign-on (10k) and a clear 12-mo manager path tied to defined milestones (team formation + delivery objectives). That keeps title honest but gives candidate runway. If hiring manager can guarantee direct reports within 6 months and HC ticket gets updated, escalate to Manager L5 with base 185–190k and higher equity.

I'll also flag HR: HC-3421 needs headcount confirmation for manager conversion. Laura, can you confirm if we have flexibility on HC timeline?

Marissa
Compensation Partner, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Candidate rec — Daniel Park (incoming L5)

Adding context from the hiring manager (forwarded below):

> From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
> Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:30:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: Hiring for Infra Serving — HC-3421
>
> We have one new headcount approved for Q3. Intended as an IC hire but team velocity is tight and I can commit to hiring two ICs in the next 12 months — the person we hire could be promoted to manager when we onboard the second IC. Not ideal but workable.

Jonas here — given the manager commitment is conditional on future hires, I'm aligned with Marissa: offer Senior IC with top-quartile base + sign-on and documented 12-month manager path. Candidate is market-active; if we want to push manager title upfront we should be ready to commit a written timeline and updated HC ticket now.

I can draft the offer language to include a manager-path appendix.

Jonas
Hiring Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@candidate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Greenleaf Talent <recruiter@greenleaf.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Inference — Offer for Senior Engineer (L5) — Daniel Park

Hi Daniel,

Thanks again for your time during the interview loop — we enjoyed the conversations and believe you'd make an excellent addition to the Infra Serving team. Below is our formal offer for the Senior Engineer (L5) role.

Offer highlights:
- Title: Senior Engineer (L5)
- Base salary: $180,000
- Sign-on bonus: $10,000 (one-time)
- Equity: RSU grant consistent with L5 top-quartile (details in doc)
- Start date: target August 28, 2028

Manager path: The hiring manager has committed to a documented Manager Path appendix that outlines objectives and a timeline to convert this role to Manager L5 when HC-3421 expands and a second IC hire is onboarded. That appendix will include milestone criteria and a 12-month review window.

Please review the attached offer packet. We're happy to discuss if you have questions about scope or the manager path.

Attachments: comp_band_reference.xlsx, headcount-ticket-3421.txt

Best,
Tessa
Staff Recruiting Partner | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@candidate.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Rivera <recruiter@greenleaf.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Inference — Offer for Senior Engineer (L5) — Daniel Park

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the prompt offer and for the manager-path appendix — I appreciate the transparency. A few quick questions before I sign:

1) If I accept as Senior Engineer (L5) with the manager-path, will I have any formal people-lead responsibilities immediately (e.g., mentoring, peer reviews) and will those feed into the manager evaluation?
2) Is there flexibility on the base to get closer to a manager L5 (185–190k) given my prior leadership stints?

I am excited about the role and want to ensure expectations align. Happy to hop on a quick call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Daniel
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 16:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Inference — Offer for Senior Engineer (L5) — Daniel Park (candidate questions)

Looping back with Daniel's questions. Suggested responses below — please confirm before I reply.

1) People responsibilities: we should state that the role will include formal mentoring and ownership of on-call rotations and that these duties will be considered in the 12-month manager evaluation.
2) Comp flexibility: is it acceptable to increase base to $185k (midpoint between top-quartile IC and manager entry) with the existing sign-on and equity, to help close? That would keep us within band tolerance and show good faith.

Marissa/Jonas/Laura — can you approve $185k base for this candidate with the manager-path appendix? If HR needs headcount confirmation to finalize manager conversion language, we should note that in the reply.

Thanks,
Tessa
